solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Betraying opinion, stifling question identifying consumer requirement?

parts.note: to shop someone is to betray them to the authorities

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: 'my bet is' means my opinion is
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: Someone giving away a view while suppressing a query, apparently identifying what a consumer needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betraying opinion' looks like one phrase but splits in two. To shop someone is British slang for informing on them; 'my bet is' means 'my opinion is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper needs something to carry purchases in, so the carrier is a requirement of anyone buying goods.

clue.text: One dislikes half-hearted contributor to top fashion?

indicators.note: half-hearted removes one of the two central letters, halving the heart of the word

parts.note: a milliner makes what goes on top of the head, playing on 'top fashion'

explanation.surface: Someone who scorns a minor player in high fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two Ts at the centre of HATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of hostility toward a thing is one who dislikes it.

clue.text: Naval officer with reduced inclination to grasp hot thing

indicators.note: to grasp means to hold, so the officer's letters enclose another

parts.note: PO is a petty officer in the navy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a bias is an inclination or leaning

explanation.surface: A sailor of rank, less keen, about to take hold of something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: PO (petty officer) is a crossword staple. 'Thing' is used as in 'having a thing about spiders'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a 'thing' about something means an irrational dread of it, an informal idiom for fear.

clue.text: Sound less inclined to escape?

definitions.meaning: sound means healthy, in fine condition
a nick is slang for a prison; an inmate of a pleasant one would be less inclined to break out

explanation.surface: A noise that seems reluctant to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison, and the phrase normally means in fine condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means healthy and in fine shape, which is what the idiom means, and literally it puts someone in a decent jail.

clue.text: First of goals worried crowd

indicators.note: First of takes only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: worried as in gnawed: something 'ate away at' or ate someone

explanation.surface: The opening goals troubled the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's eating you?' shows worried = ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports attendance figure is called the gate, the size of the crowd that paid to get in.

clue.text: Cheers up, about to enter restaurant to engage in seduction?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you, like cheers

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Thanks are given, and someone is about to go into a restaurant to woo a date.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks, and 'up' reads it bottom to top in this down entry. A trat is a trattoria.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or draw someone in is what a seducer does, so drawing a person's interest is engaging in seduction.

clue.text: This, by the way, is appropriate behaviour

definitions.text: This, by the way, is appropriate behaviour

parts.words: This, by the way, is appropriate behaviour
parts.note: 'by the way' reads literally as beside the road: the routine children learn for crossing a street safely

explanation.surface: An aside that some conduct is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like an aside but means at the roadside. The kerb is the British name for the curb at the pavement edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside safety drill taught to children is the proper behaviour beside a road.

clue.text: Such a blow, with touch of calamity, could result in this shock defeat

indicators.note: could result in signals that these letters, rearranged, give the answer together with another bit
touch of means just a small trace: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A blow that, with a hint of disaster, could cause a stunning loss.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of THIS SHOCK DEFEAT equal the answer plus C, the first letter of 'calamity'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal, ruinous blow to someone's chances is called this idiom, as if a lethal embrace.

clue.text: Nasty fight with adversary when there are fewer people around?

definitions.text: when there are fewer people around?

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ugly brawl with an enemy at a quiet time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' scrambles FIGHT and ADVERSARY together.
explanation.definitionFit: The overnight work period is when few are awake and about, a shift named after the deserted cemetery.

clue.text: Again pondered about allowing it at last

parts.note: re means about, concerning
allowing that means though, granting

indicators.note: at last picks just the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone mulled it over again, concerning permitting it after all.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something a second time is to reconsider it, past tense to match 'pondered'.

clue.text: Short male escaping charge (electric primarily)

indicators.note: escaping means getting out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: terms are the charges or fees asked

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A short man getting away from an electric charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' removes M from TERMS, leaving TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, brief speech is clipped and short, a synonym.

clue.text: Medic about right, with one attempt to determine source of giddiness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the vet's letters go round another

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
I is the Roman numeral one
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A doctor, being about right, has one try at diagnosing what causes dizziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside VET.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear of heights causes dizziness, so the condition is a cause of a spinning head.

clue.text: Core elements of rights presented by current proponent of independence

parts.note: the two central letters of 'rights' are G and H, spelt out with the word 'and' between them
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The essence of rights is offered by a modern champion of self-rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of 'rights' is G and H, and the 'and' is kept as letters: 'G and H'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian leader campaigned for India's freedom from British rule, a champion of self-government.

clue.text: Hesitation over a limited broadcast on various channels

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pause before a restricted transmission on several channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns UM to MU; 'broadcast' rearranges LIMITED to LTIMEDI, with A from the clue at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Content delivered in several forms at once, such as text, sound and video, uses many different media.

clue.text: Supporting Vote Republican for a time

parts.note: a yea is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: Backing the Republican candidate for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months is a period, one measured span of time.

clue.text: A synthetic flower looking very white?

parts.note: lab-made means synthetic, made in a laboratory
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: An artificial bloom that looks extremely pale.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale stone gives the phrase 'alabaster skin', so it describes something extremely white.

clue.text: American attempts to get behind independent businesses

indicators.note: to get behind means to follow, so these pieces come after

parts.note: tries are attempts

explanation.surface: An American tries to support independent firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Branches of trade or manufacturing are sectors of commerce, as in 'the oil industry'.

clue.text: Freshly deploy material recently restricting military commander

parts.note: material means real, relevant, substantial

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: late means recently, as in 'of late'
OC is Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: Redeploy recent material that hems in a commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is the adjective meaning relevant or real, not cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign resources anew is to deploy them again in a different way.

clue.text: Almost lean over, with a quantity of yielding

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a ship lists when it leans over to one side
some means a quantity of

explanation.surface: Nearly bending over, with a measure of give.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and flexible, bending easily, is yielding.

clue.text: Reduced opening for staff symbol

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a cleft is a split or opening

explanation.surface: Smaller access for a sign used by employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign at the start of a musical stave fixes the pitch of the notes on its lines.

clue.text: Finally being the sole provider?

definitions.meaning: finally means eventually, in the end
a cobbler's last is the foot-shaped block on which soles are fitted, so something there gets a sole

explanation.surface: Eventually becoming the only breadwinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' is the bottom of a shoe, not 'only'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, and literally places a shoe on the cobbler's mould where soles are attached.

clue.text: Shilling in reserve is not very substantial

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a spare is kept in reserve
S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A shilling held back is not much money.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and scanty, meagre in amount, is not very substantial.

clue.text: Gas: average energy including couple of therms?

indicators.note: including means containing, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the mean is an average

indicators.note: couple of picks the first two letters of the next word

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gas reading of average energy covering a couple of therms on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts TH inside MEANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas used for heating is mostly this simple hydrocarbon.

clue.text: A small photo showing lavender

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

explanation.surface: A tiny photograph of lavender.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides the savoury jelly, the word names spike lavender.
explanation.definitionFit: Spike lavender, a species of the plant, is also known by this name, a lesser-known sense.

clue.text: Snack with clout?

parts.note: a clout is a blow, a rap

explanation.surface: A snack with real weight behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla rolled round a filling is a light meal, a kind of snack.

clue.text: Opening in Test, but only opening, getting run out

indicators.note: only opening means just the first letter of the word

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A batsman at the start of a Test, only opening, is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: The introductory passage of a piece of music or a talk is its opening.

clue.text: Descriptive of special treatment favoured by Yorkshire resort

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Special treatment preferred by a seaside town in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: VIPs are welcomed by a carpet rolled out, so the phrase describes lavish, privileged handling.

clue.text: No aimless activity for selected doctors?

definitions.meaning: shooting at a mark to improve aim is anything but aimless
a surgery of doctors that has been selected or aimed at would be a targeted practice

explanation.surface: Purposeful work by hand-picked physicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' also means a group of doctors, here one that has been targeted.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting drill at a bullseye is focused aiming, and a picked medical surgery is a practice that is the chosen object.
